standard.title: Divide with remainders
standard.description: Solve problems involving division, choosing efficient strategies and using digital tools where appropriate; interpret any remainder according to the context and express results as a whole number, decimal or fraction
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can apply estimation and rounding strategies (AC9M4N07). They have not yet interpreted remainders in context or expressed division results as decimals or fractions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students solve problems involving division using efficient strategies and interpret any remainder as a whole number, decimal or fraction according to context.

nodes.label: Division strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply and explain at least two division strategies for dividing multi-digit numbers.
nodes.minimum_width: Divide a two- or three-digit number by a single digit using at least one written strategy; show working.
nodes.typical_width: Apply and compare strategies: short division, repeated subtraction, partition; use digital tools to verify; identify efficient strategies for different number types.
wider: Connect division to multiplication inverse: 144 ÷ 12 via 12 × ? = 144

response_modes.reason: Students with only one strategy are vulnerable when divisors are large or numbers are awkward. A repertoire including informal and formal methods builds flexibility.

success_criteria: Student applies a division strategy correctly to a multi-digit ÷ single-digit problem
Student can explain the steps in their chosen strategy

nodes.label: Interpreting remainders
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret a remainder in three ways (whole number remainder, decimal, fraction) according to context.
nodes.minimum_width: Solve a division problem with a remainder and explain the remainder as both a whole number leftover and as a fraction of the divisor.
nodes.typical_width: Solve problems in varied contexts where the same remainder requires different interpretations (round up, round down, express as decimal, express as fraction); explain the contextual reasoning for each choice.
wider: Investigate how digital tools represent remainders and why the representation choice matters
Explore Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander contexts involving proportional sharing that require remainder interpretation

response_modes.reason: Remainder interpretation is entirely context-dependent. Students who only practise one form (whole number remainder) fail to transfer. Multiple contrasting contexts are the only way to build the required interpretive judgement.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The variety of contextual remainder interpretations is genuinely rich: sharing food, packaging, rounding costs. Advancing students benefit from designing their own contextual problems.
nodes.hinge_reason: Remainder interpretation is required in Node 3 — students who can only express remainders in one form cannot select the appropriate representation when choosing a strategy for a given problem context.
success_criteria: Student interprets a remainder correctly as directed by context
Student explains why the same remainder might be expressed differently in different contexts

nodes.label: Choosing strategies and digital tools
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can choose an efficient division strategy for a given problem and use digital tools appropriately.
nodes.minimum_width: Select a division strategy appropriate for a given problem and explain the choice; use a digital tool to verify the result.
nodes.typical_width: Compare efficiency of mental, written and digital strategies across different problem types; justify strategy selection; apply in multi-step contexts.
wider: Investigate when digital tools are more appropriate than written strategies and vice versa
Apply division strategy selection to financial problem contexts

response_modes.reason: Efficient strategy selection for division requires a repertoire of approaches. Students who only know one strategy cannot adapt — breadth of strategies is the learning.

success_criteria: Student selects an appropriate strategy for a given division problem
Student explains why the chosen strategy is efficient
